title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026
subtitle:
140 crore Indians take pride having navigated world crises effectively, and that despite these headwinds India's growth has remained robust: PM

The future of energy security lies in clean energy: PM

This new era of the solar revolution is not just about adoption, it is equally driven by innovation: PM

I strongly urge our startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs to develop models that ensure the maximum energy needs of a household are fulfilled through solar power: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Addressing the gathering of industry leaders, investors, startup representatives, and senior officials from India and abroad, the Prime Minister noted that this year's summit takes place amid special circumstances dominated by global energy shocks that have underscored the vital importance of renewable energy in daily life and national development. He pointed out that the scope of this year's event is exceptionally broad as it coincides with the Ninth Assembly of the International Solar Alliance and includes delegates from the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen.
Observing that the global economy has weathered unprecedented disruptions ranging from the Corona pandemic to the ongoing West Asia crisis, the Prime Minister stated that 140 crore Indians take pride in how effectively the nation has managed the turmoil while maintaining high economic growth. He emphasized that ten years of sustained domestic investment and systemic reforms in clean energy shielded the country from severe external shocks. “If India had not invested in clean energy and created new systems for this over the past decade, then our crisis could have been much more severe than the rest of the world,” noted PM Modi.
Stating that recent global disruptions have demonstrated the direct link between energy security and economic security, the Prime Minister warned that continued over-reliance on fossil fuels will repeatedly disrupt the world economy because fossil reserves are finite and concentrated in a few regions. He contrasted this vulnerability with the boundless, universally accessible potential of clean energy. “And we all know, the future of Energy Security lies in Clean Energy,” asserted Shri Modi.
Describing India's 12-year clean energy journey as one defined by Promises, Passion, and Performance exemplified by its COP-26 commitment to achieve 500 Gigawatts of non-fossil capacity by 2030, the Prime Minister highlighted that the nation fulfilled its Paris pledge of sourcing half its installed power capacity from non-fossil sources in 2025, five years ahead of schedule. Noting that India now ranks among the top three nations in solar and renewable energy with over 50 percent non-fossil installed capacity and nearly 300 Gigawatts already achieved toward the 500-Gigawatt target, he announced an ambitious goal to add another 500 Gigawatts of new non-fossil capacity over the next 10 to 11 years. “This target is somewhat difficult, but I have faith in the capability of my country; therefore I say, We will do it!” affirmed PM Modi.
Emphasizing that India wishes to share the benefits of its innovations and experiences with all of humanity, the Prime Minister stated that the nation approaches green energy with the same cooperative spirit before presenting specific examples. “The successes of India in this field will come in handy for numerous countries of the world,” remarked Shri Modi.
Detailing the rapid progress of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana launched in February 2024 to install rooftop solar panels in one crore homes, the Prime Minister noted that over 65 lakh households have joined the movement within 24 to 25 months at a pace of one lakh new homes every six days, cutting electricity bills by roughly 76 percent according to a study and reducing bills to zero for lakhs of families who now earn money by selling surplus power to the grid. “This scheme of India can give great strength to energy security in many countries,” observed PM Modi.
Highlighting efforts over the past 12 years to integrate solar power into daily life, industry, and agriculture, the Prime Minister pointed out that connecting over 44,000 government buildings with solar energy is saving nearly 700 crore rupees annually, while the KUSUM scheme has provided solar irrigation to over 30 lakh farmers and saved each solar pump beneficiary nearly one lakh rupees every year. He also cited the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, which installs solar panels over reservoirs, ponds, and lakes to optimize water bodies and save land acquisition costs. “India is making solar power a part of the lives of its citizens,” noted Shri Modi.
Stating that India's clean energy ecosystem extends beyond hydro, solar, wind, and nuclear power, the Prime Minister explained that the country is advancing in mission mode under the National Green Hydrogen Mission to produce 50 lakh tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of the decade while integrating green hydrogen into the transport sector. “Just a few months ago, India started its first Green Hydrogen Train,” noted PM Modi.
Acknowledging that power generation must be matched by efficient distribution from high-production solar and wind zones to regions with lower output so that homes, farms, and industries across the country benefit equally, the Prime Minister highlighted the development of Green Energy Corridors comprising dedicated transmission lines and substations supported by the One Nation, One Power Grid network that unified five regional grids onto a single frequency. He added that the country is now advancing to the next phase to further strengthen this transmission infrastructure. “Recently, India has set a target of an investment of about 2 lakh crore rupees for this,” observed Shri Modi.
Attributing India's green energy success to a dramatic surge in domestic manufacturing after years of complete import dependence for even minor solar components, the Prime Minister noted that solar module manufacturing capacity has grown from around 2 Gigawatts a decade ago to over 200 Gigawatts today alongside nearly 40 Gigawatts of solar cell capacity and expanding production of other components. “Meaning, India's ambitions related to green energy are also proof of the success of our Atmanirbhar Bharat campaign and the Make in India campaign,” asserted PM Modi.
Stressing that the nation must maintain its rapid momentum rather than resting on its laurels, the Prime Minister called for swiftly connecting every government building, school, college, hospital, and streetlight network to solar energy. He proposed fostering healthy competition among states and local bodies to incentivize top performers and enable peer learning from local success stories. “We have to do this work at a fast pace,” asserted Shri Modi.
Offering a dedicated suggestion for expanding solar power in agriculture, the Prime Minister urged moving beyond the distribution of lakhs of solar pumps to utilizing uncultivated farm spaces. He emphasized the need to encourage farmers across maximum villages to install solar panels on vacant land as well as along farm boundary ridges. “We have to move beyond solar pumps,” remarked PM Modi.
Stating that the new era of the solar revolution relies on innovation as much as adoption, the Prime Minister urged startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs to design round-the-clock, all-weather solar models capable of meeting maximum household needs, including rooftop solar cooking to minimize reliance on imported gas and home solar charging for electric two-wheelers and cars. “Through this, middle-class families of the country can save thousands of rupees every year,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the need for specialized clean energy applications in rural allied sectors, the Prime Minister called for developing dedicated solar products to promote solar power in the dairy sector. “For animal fodder, crop harvesting, and post-harvest, solar equipment should be developed for every such work,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that achieving these goals requires next-generation innovation, indigenous storage hardware, and new battery storage capacity, the Prime Minister described this need as a massive opportunity for India's youth and urged researchers and investors to seize the moment. “The solutions that you prepare in India will come in handy for numerous countries of the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Pointing out that every clean energy initiative in one of the world's youngest nations is generating thousands of jobs across panel and hardware manufacturing, installation, servicing, and transportation, the Prime Minister noted that further expansion of solar capacity will multiply employment opportunities across the economy. “From the kitchen stove to the means of transport, when everything is solar-power-driven and green-energy-driven, then a new industry will be created,” observed PM Modi.
Inviting global investors to leverage India's unmatched demand, scale, scope, and political and policy stability, the Prime Minister noted that the renewable energy sector has attracted over 15 lakh crore rupees, or 164 billion dollars, over the past decade, including over 6 lakh crore rupees, or 63 billion dollars, in just the two years since the 2024 RE-INVEST Summit, with investment opportunities projected to exceed 20 lakh crore rupees, or 220 billion dollars, by the end of the decade. “Therefore, for all of you, a new sky of opportunities is going to open up in India's clean energy sector,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recalling India's global message of One Earth, One Family, One Future that underpins both its clean energy journey and the International Solar Alliance, the Prime Minister stated that the nation is committed to ensuring necessary funding, technology, and expertise reach every country in need. “Therefore, for Africa, a proposal for a 200 million dollar Africa Solar Facility has been put forward,” noted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that the coming decade is vital for global climate goals, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that summit participants will play a pivotal role in securing the future by connecting every country and region to this transformation before concluding with his best wishes. “Only then will we be able to build a Clean Future, a Green Future, and a Secure Future,” asserted Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo in Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister in my Cabinet, Pralhad Joshi ji, Shripad Naik ji, all industry leaders, investors, colleagues from the startup world, senior officials, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from India and abroad.
I welcome and greet all of you to the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit. This year's summit is special because it is being held under special circumstances. We have seen how this year has largely been dominated by discussions around energy shocks. The importance of renewable energy in our lives and in our development journey has become even clearer this year. It is also a happy coincidence that the 9th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance is being held alongside this summit. Delegates attending the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen are also present here. That means the scale of this year's event is very large. I extend my best wishes to all of you.
Friends,
Over the past few years, the global economy has witnessed unprecedented crises. From the COVID pandemic to the West Asia crisis, the world has faced several major challenges, and the crisis in West Asia is still continuing. But 140 crore Indians feel proud that we have handled these challenges better than many others, and despite these crises, India's growth has remained high. Had India not invested in clean energy and not established new systems in this sector over the past decade, our crisis could have been far more severe than that faced by the rest of the world.
Friends,
This global crisis has delivered a clear message to every country: energy security is directly linked to economic security. And we all know that the future of energy security lies in clean energy. If we continue to remain excessively dependent on fossil fuels, the global economy will continue to face repeated disruptions. Fossil fuel reserves are limited and concentrated in only a few regions. Renewable energy, on the other hand, has unlimited potential, and every region and every country can benefit from it.
Friends,
India's journey in this sector over the past twelve years has been one of promises, passion, and performance. The proof of this is our commitment made at COP-26. At the 2021 Summit, India resolved to achieve 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. We said: We will do it! In our Paris pledge, India had also set the goal of meeting half of its installed power capacity through non-fossil sources. India achieved that target itself in 2025. In other words, we achieved it five years ahead of schedule. Today, more than 50 percent of our installed power capacity is based on non-fossil sources. India is also progressing firmly towards the target of 500 gigawatts. We have already achieved nearly 300 gigawatts. And today, India is among the top three countries in the world in solar and renewable energy. Over the next ten to eleven years, our effort is to add another 500 gigawatts of new non-fossil fuel capacity. This target is somewhat challenging, but I have full confidence in the capabilities of my country. And therefore, I say: We will do it!
Friends,
We want India's innovations and India's experiences to benefit all humanity. This is also our approach towards green energy. India's successes in this field can be useful to many countries around the world. I will explain this through examples.
Friends,
In February 2024, we launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. Under this scheme, the target is to install rooftop solar panels on one crore homes. In just the past twenty-four to twenty-five months, more than sixty-five lakh homes have joined this campaign. And as our Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi ji just mentioned, every six days, one lakh new homes become part of this solar movement. The impact of this can also be seen in electricity bills. One study shows that electricity bills for these sixty-five lakh households have fallen by nearly 76 percent. There are lakhs of families whose electricity bills have become zero. There are also many families that are generating surplus electricity and earning income by selling it back to the grid. This scheme can significantly strengthen energy security in many countries, especially in the Global South.
Friends,
India is making solar power a part of the lives of its citizens. Over the past twelve years, we have also tried to connect industries and farms with solar power. More than 44,000 government buildings in India are now connected to solar energy. This is saving nearly ₹700 crore annually. India's farmers are also benefiting greatly from the KUSUM Scheme. Through it, more than 30 lakh farmers have received access to solar-powered irrigation. It is estimated that every farmer benefiting from a solar pump is saving nearly one lakh rupees every year. Let me also give you the example of the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana. Its concept is to generate electricity by installing solar panels on ponds, lakes, and reservoirs. This allows better utilisation of water bodies. Such projects also reduce the costs associated with acquiring land.
Friends,
Our clean energy ecosystem is not limited only to hydro, solar, wind, and nuclear energy. India is moving in mission mode to take a major leap in the field of green hydrogen. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, we have set a target of producing five million tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of this decade. We are also connecting our transport sector with green hydrogen. Just a few months ago, India launched its first Green Hydrogen Train.
Friends,
All of you experts know that merely generating electricity is not enough. It is equally important to distribute it efficiently and deliver it where it is needed. In India, solar and wind energy are generated more abundantly in certain regions. We must ensure that areas where power generation is relatively low also benefit from it, so that homes, farms, and industries there can also run on clean power. That is why Green Energy Corridors are being developed. Under these corridors, a dedicated network of transmission lines and substations is being established. This is making it easier to transfer solar and wind power from places of production to places of demand. And in this effort, the contribution of One Nation, One Power Grid has been immense. Over the years, we have integrated five regional grids into a single national network. Today, the entire country is connected through a power grid operating at a common frequency. To further strengthen this Green Energy Corridor system, we have now moved to the next phase. Recently, India set an investment target of nearly ₹2 lakh crore for this purpose.
Friends,
A major reason behind our success in green energy is also our growing manufacturing capacity. Until a few years ago, we were completely dependent on imports even for the smallest components related to solar energy. A decade ago, our solar module manufacturing capacity was only around 2 gigawatts. Today, it has crossed 200 gigawatts. Solar cell manufacturing capacity has also reached nearly 40 gigawatts. We are now expanding the manufacturing of other components as well. In other words, India's ambitions in green energy are also proof of the success of our Atmanirbhar Bharat mission and the success of the Make in India campaign.
Friends,
India is striving to achieve a great deal within a very short span of time. We cannot stop here. We must connect every government building, every school and college, every hospital, and the entire street-lighting system to solar energy, and we must do so at a rapid pace. I would suggest that healthy competition should be encouraged among states and local bodies, so that those who perform better can be rewarded and others can learn from their success stories.
Friends,
I have a suggestion related to solar power in agriculture as well. We have distributed millions of solar pumps, but we now need to move beyond solar pumps. My vision is that the Annadata should also become an Urjadata - the food provider should become an energy provider. Farmers should install solar panels on unused land. Even the boundaries of fields should not remain unused; solar panels should be installed there as well. We must ensure that this reaches as many villages as possible.
Friends,
This new phase of the solar revolution is not only about adoption; it also depends on innovation. Therefore, I make a special appeal to our startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs: come forward and create models where as many household needs as possible can be met through solar power. We need solutions that make solar power available twenty-four hours a day and in every season. We must move towards a situation where a family can cook food using electricity generated by the solar plant installed on its own rooftop. We need to launch a clean cooking movement. Dependence on imported gas should be reduced as much as possible. We must also create a situation where a larger number of middle-class families have the option of electric vehicles and can charge their scooters, bikes, and cars at home using electricity generated from their own solar systems. This can save middle-class families thousands of rupees every year.
Friends,
We also need products that promote solar power in the dairy sector. Solar-powered equipment should be developed for every activity, from preparing animal feed to harvesting crops and post-harvest operations.
Friends,
None of this will be possible without next-generation innovation. For this, the country needs the necessary hardware. We need indigenous storage solutions. We need to build new battery storage capacity. This is a tremendous opportunity for all of you and for the youth of the country. I urge everyone in the world of research and all investors not to let this opportunity pass by. The solutions you develop in India will serve many countries around the world.
Friends,
India is one of the youngest countries in the world, and every effort in clean energy is creating large numbers of new employment opportunities. Even today, thousands and thousands of people are finding jobs in this sector, and there is tremendous potential for green jobs. These opportunities are being created across different fields, from manufacturing panels and other hardware to installation, servicing, and transportation. In the future, as solar power capacity increases further, just imagine how many more jobs will be created. From kitchen stoves to transportation systems, when everything becomes solar-powered and green-energy-driven, an entirely new industry will emerge.
Friends,
For all of you, for investors across the world, India is opening up enormous opportunities. It is difficult to find elsewhere the kind of demand, scale, and scope that India offers. It is equally difficult to find the kind of political and policy stability that India provides. And we are seeing the results of this. Over the past decade, more than ₹15 lakh crore, that is, 164 billion dollars, has been invested in the renewable energy sector. From the RE-INVEST Summit of 2024 until today, within just two years, investments worth nearly ₹6 lakh crore, that is, more than 63 billion dollars, have come into this sector. It is estimated that by the end of this decade, investment opportunities worth more than ₹20 lakh crore, approximately 220 billion dollars, will be created in this sector. Therefore, a new horizon of opportunities is opening up for all of you in India’s clean energy sector.
Friends,
India has given the world the message of One Earth, One Family, One Future. The same philosophy is reflected in our clean energy journey. This is the thinking behind the International Solar Alliance. Our effort is to ensure that the funding, technology, and expertise required for renewable energy reach every country that needs them. That is why a proposal has been put forward for a 200-million-dollar Africa Solar Facility for Africa.
Friends,
The coming decade is extremely important for our climate goals. And I am confident that everyone present at this summit will play a major role in securing that future. We must connect every country to this mission. Every region must become a participant in this transformation. Only then will we be able to build a clean future, a green future, and a secure future. With these words, I once again extend my heartfelt best wishes to all of you.
Thank you.

title: PM to Inaugurate and Lay Foundation Stone of Pune Metro Projects Worth Around ₹21,800 Crore on 3rd November
subtitle:
PM to Inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3 (Pink Line), Built at a Cost of Over ₹8,300 Crore

Pink Line to Provide Metro Connectivity Between Hinjewadi IT Hub and Shivajinagar

Pune Metro Line 3 to be Operated Entirely by Women Train Operators; Around 30% of Electricity Requirements to be Met Through Solar Power

PM to Lay Foundation Stone of Pune Metro Phase-II, Comprising Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, at an Estimated Cost of Around ₹13,500 Crore

Pune Metro Phase-II to Expand Connectivity Across Major Residential, Commercial and IT Hubs

New Metro Corridors to Integrate with Existing Pune Metro Network and Intercity Bus Services, Enhancing Urban Connectivity
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around ₹21,800 crore on 3rd November 2026 at 12:30 PM through video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over ₹8,300 crore. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune's urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportation solutions.
Spanning approximately 23 kilometres, the Pink Line connects Maan to District Court Metro station. The corridor will provide Metro connectivity between the Hinjewadi IT hub and Shivajinagar, improving access to one of Pune's major employment centres and facilitating the daily commute of thousands of IT professionals and other commuters. The corridor will integrate with the existing metro network, providing seamless connectivity across different parts of Pune. It will help reduce dependence on private vehicles, ease traffic congestion and vehicular emissions, and improve access to major commercial and residential areas.
A notable feature of the Pink Line is its emphasis on women's empowerment and gender-inclusive public transportation. The line will be operated entirely by women train operators, making it a first-of-its-kind initiative. The project also emphasises environmental sustainability, with approximately 30% of its total electricity requirements envisaged to be met through solar power.
Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone of Phase-II of Pune Metro, to be developed at an estimated cost of around ₹13,500 crore. Phase-II comprises Pune Metro Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, which will substantially expand the city's Metro network and strengthen connectivity across important residential, commercial and IT hubs.
Under Phase-II, Lines 2A and 2B will span a total length of around 12.75 kilometres. Line 2A will connect Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, while Line 2B will connect Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, extending the existing east-west Metro network. Line 4, spanning around 25.52 kilometres, will connect Kharadi to Khadakwasla. Line 4A, spanning 6.12 kilometres, will connect Nal Stop to Manik Baug.
The new Metro corridors will connect several important locations, including Kharadi, Magarpatta, Hadapsar, Swargate, Manik Baug, Nanded City, Pune Cantonment and Warje. The eastern extension from Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi will improve connectivity to rapidly developing residential, commercial and IT hubs in Kharadi and Wagholi. The corridors will integrate with intercity bus services and the existing Pune Metro network through interchange facilities at Swargate, Nal Stop and Kharadi Bypass, facilitating seamless connectivity across different parts of the city.
These projects will strengthen Pune's public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON LAWMAKERS TO UPHOLD DISSENT AS A STRENGTH OF DEMOCRACY
subtitle:
LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES LAWMAKERS TO REMAIN FOCUSED ON SERVING THE LAST PERSON IN SOCIETY

HARYANA’S SIX-DECADE DEVELOPMENT JOURNEY STANDS AS A SHINING TESTAMENT TO STRENGTH AND RESILIENCE OF INDIA’S DEMOCRACY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

CONSTITUTION IS NOT MERELY A GOVERNING FRAMEWORK, BUT LIVING SOUL AND MORAL COMPASS OF INDIA: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES ‘JANPRATINIDHI SAMMELAN’ ORGANISED BY HARYANA VIDHAN SABHA AT PANCHKULA AS PART OF SAMVIDHAN PAKHWADA PROGRAMME
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that agreement and disagreement are two sides of the same coin in a healthy and vibrant democracy. He stressed that dissent must be welcomed and respected as a vital catalyst for bringing fresh perspectives, addressing administrative blind spots and promoting better governance. He underscored that, irrespective of political, party or ideological differences, the overarching commitment of all public representatives must remain the continued progress of the State and the nation.
Shri Birla made these remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the ‘Janpratinidhi Sammelan’, organised by the Haryana Vidhan Sabha at Panchkula today as part of the Samvidhan Pakhwada Programme. Addressing serving and former members of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha, along with former ministers, he reflected on Haryana’s six-decade journey of growth, socio-economic resilience and leadership across multiple sectors, placing the State’s remarkable achievements firmly within the framework of India’s constitutional values and democratic ethos.
Reflecting on the State’s evolution over the past sixty years, Shri Birla observed that Haryana has consistently remained at the forefront of national progress despite numerous historical and administrative challenges. Drawing parallels with the timeless message of karma enshrined in the Bhagavad Gita, he lauded the farming community for pioneering the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, enhancing crop yields and contributing significantly to the country's food security. He also praised Haryana’s youth in the armed forces for their exemplary valour in safeguarding the nation's borders and internal security. He also commended  Haryana’s sportspersons for consistently enhancing India's stature on the global sporting stage.
Highlighting the inclusive and deliberative nature of India's constitutional journey, Shri Birla noted that the Constituent Assembly, under the guidance of the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and with the participation of distinguished leaders from different regions, including Haryana and Punjab, laid the foundations of a cohesive parliamentary democracy amid immense linguistic, cultural and religious diversity. He emphasised that the survival and flourishing of India's diverse federal polity stand as a global testament to the resilience of its democracy. He observed, “Our Constitution is not merely a framework for running the government; it is the soul of India, reflecting our national consciousness and the aspirations of crores of people.”
Shri Birla emphasised that the commitment to public service does not end with the completion of one's tenure in the Legislature. He urged lawmakers to regard governance and administration primarily as instruments of grassroots empowerment rather than merely as administrative mechanisms. He stated that the ultimate measure of political and social life lies in bringing tangible socio-economic transformation and genuine happiness to the lives of the most vulnerable sections of society—the last person in the queue.
Shri Birla also appreciated the Haryana Legislative Assembly for setting an exemplary benchmark over its six-decade parliamentary journey through high-quality debates, reasoned dialogue and adherence to legislative dignity. He noted that the Assembly has served as an inspiration for legislative bodies across the country, demonstrating that democratic institutions become stronger when they remain firmly rooted in public welfare and institutional accountability.
The event was also graced by Chief Minister of Haryana Shri Nayab Singh Saini; Speaker of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Shri Harvinder Kalyan; Leader of the Opposition in the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Shri Bhupinder Singh Hooda; Parliamentary Affairs Minister of Haryana Shri Mahipal Dhanda; and Deputy Speaker of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Dr. Krishan Lal Middha.
हरियाणा विधानसभा में ‘संविधान पखवाड़ा 2026’ के अंतर्गत आयोजित ‘जनप्रतिनिधि सम्मेलन’ को संबोधित किया। हरियाणा के वर्तमान एवं पूर्व विधायकों की सहभागिता वाला यह सम्मेलन अनुभवों और विचारों के आदान-प्रदान तथा लोकतांत्रिक परंपराओं को और सुदृढ़ करने का महत्वपूर्ण अवसर रहा। 

श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता की पावन भूमि हरियाणा ने अपनी विकास यात्रा में परिश्रम, साहस और समर्पण के बल पर राष्ट्र के विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में उल्लेखनीय योगदान दिया है। भारत का संविधान हमारे स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के आदर्शों और देश की सामूहिक आकांक्षाओं का प्रतिबिंब है। बाबा साहब डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर सहित संविधान सभा के सदस्यों के योगदान से निर्मित यह संविधान न्याय, स्वतंत्रता, समानता और बंधुता के मूल्यों के माध्यम से हमारे लोकतंत्र को दिशा देता है। हमारे लोकतंत्र की शक्ति जनता के विश्वास और उसकी भागीदारी में निहित है। 

संसद से लेकर विधानसभाओं और पंचायतों तक प्रत्येक जनप्रतिनिधि का दायित्व है कि वह जनता की अपेक्षाओं को सदन तक पहुँचाए, जनहित के विषयों को प्राथमिकता दे और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं की गरिमा बनाए रखे। पूर्व विधायकों का अनुभव और वर्तमान जनप्रतिनिधियों की ऊर्जा इस दायित्व को और प्रभावी बना सकती है। विचारों में भिन्नता लोकतंत्र का स्वाभाविक हिस्सा है, लेकिन संवाद तथा सहमति और असहमति के परस्पर सम्मान से ही हम साझा उद्देश्यों की ओर आगे बढ़ सकते हैं।

title: 1st International Maize Conference 2026 Calls for Higher Productivity, Innovative Breeding and Farmer-Centric Research
subtitle:
Research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods: Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE  

Dr. Jat advocates Systems-Science Approach to Bridge Yield Gaps and Strategically Target Maize Across Seasons Without Compromising Oilseeds and Pulses
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 1st International Maize Conference themed “Maize Revolution for Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Sustainability in the Changing World,” (M4FS) commenced at the JD Convention Centre, Hyderabad today, bringing together scientists, policymakers, agricultural institutions and industry stakeholders to discuss strategies for advancing maize research, productivity and value-chain development.
The conference highlighted high-yielding varieties and hybrids, improved nutritional quality, efficient resource utilisation, mechanisation, robust seed systems and maize’s growing role in food, feed, fodder and energy security.
Addressing the conference Secretary, DARE and DG ICAR Dr. M. L. Jat, congratulated the maize research community on India’s maize production reaching approximately 55 million tonnes, accompanied by substantial productivity gains over the past decade. He called for increasing production to 75 million tonnes over the next decade, alongside a further 1.5-fold increase in productivity through technological innovation, improved crop management and efficient resource utilisation.
Emphasising an expansion of the traditional 4F vision—Food, Feed, Fodder and Fuel—to 5F by placing Farmers at the centre, Dr. Jat stressed that research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods. He advocated a systems-science approach to bridging yield gaps, particularly those arising from crop management, and strategic targeting of maize across seasons and agroecological zones without compromising other important crops, particularly oilseeds and pulses. He also underscored the need for affordable, quality seed, especially public-sector hybrids, supported by a robust seed system.
Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR, described maize as a model crop for food, nutritional and energy security. Acknowledging progress in maize research and extension over the past five years, including the development of 329 maize hybrids, he called for strengthening the All India Coordinated Research Project on Maize (AICRP on Maize). He emphasised breeding for higher yields, improved nutritional quality and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, alongside input-use efficiency, mechanisation, capacity development and stronger public-sector hybrid seed production. He also highlighted the need for collaboration among research institutions, universities and industry to realise maize’s potential as an ethanol feedstock.
Padma Shri Dr. S. Vasal, eminent maize scientist and a World Food Laurete associated with CIMMYT, advocated simple, cost-effective breeding approaches to accelerate the development of improved varieties and hybrids suited to farmers’ needs.
Padma Bhushan Dr. R. S. Paroda, former Secretary, DARE, and Director General, ICAR, and Chief Guest, stressed the importance of aligning research priorities with the evolving needs of agriculture and allied sectors. He called for greater use of advanced breeding techniques, systematic germplasm conservation and utilisation, stronger maize value chains, and effective aflatoxin management to ensure maize safety and quality for food and feed.
Earlier, Dr. H. S. Jat, President, Maize Technologists Association of India (MTAI), welcomed the dignitaries and highlighted maize’s strategic importance in India’s agricultural transformation. He called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, agricultural universities, policymakers and industry to address emerging challenges.
Several scientific publications were released during the programme, and awards were presented to eminent scientists and researchers in recognition of their contributions to maize research and development.
The conference underscored the importance of collaborative, farmer-centric research to bridge yield gaps, improve seed access, strengthen breeding programmes, enhance nutritional quality and develop sustainable maize value chains. Being held from 2–4 November, 2026 in Hyderabad, the conference provides a platform for national and international experts to shape a roadmap for a productive, profitable and sustainable maize sector in India.

content:
The Ministry of Coal today successfully hosted the Annual Star Rating Awards Ceremony for FY 2024-25 in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, recognising excellence and outstanding performance in India's coal and lignite mining sector. The ceremony was graced by the Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, in the presence of senior officials of the Ministry, representatives of Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited, Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), and other stakeholders from the coal industry.
A total of 50 coal mines received Five-Star Ratings for FY 2024-25. Among these, 10 mines secured the first, second and third positions in their respective categories, with scores exceeding 93 per cent. Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) and NTPC secured the First Prize in the Opencast category, while Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) secured the First Prize in the Underground category. Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) received special appreciation for achieving the highest number of Five-Star Rated mines among all Coal India subsidiaries. Northern Coalfields Limited and Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) were also appreciated for consistently maintaining high performance in Star Rating evaluations as well as production.
Addressing the Star Rating Awards Ceremony for FY 2024-25, the Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines emphasized that the Star Rating Programme serves as an important instrument for promoting healthy competition among coal mines and motivating them to continually improve their performance. He encouraged coal companies to view the programme not merely as an assessment exercise but as an opportunity for self-evaluation, learning and improvement. He highlighted the importance of adopting best practices, strengthening mine operations, maintaining proper records and embracing modern and safer technologies to enhance overall mining performance.
Congratulating the award-winning mines and their teams, the Union Minister of State appreciated their dedication and commitment towards achieving higher standards. He also acknowledged the consistent performance of mines in various categories and encouraged other mining establishments to draw inspiration from their achievements. Calling for wider and more active participation in the Star Rating Programme for FY 2025-26, he stressed that healthy competition, continuous self-improvement and the exchange of good practices would help raise performance standards across the coal sector and advance the vision of safe, efficient and sustainable mining.
In his keynote, Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, highlighted the evolution of the Star Rating Programme as an important platform for recognising performance and institutionalising best practices across the coal mining sector. He noted that the Ministry has consistently strengthened this platform through successive award ceremonies, providing recognition to mines demonstrating exemplary performance. He emphasised that such structured assessment and recognition play an important role in setting benchmarks, encouraging transparency and creating opportunities for mines to learn from demonstrated excellence.
Referring to the achievements for FY 2024-25, Shri Jha noted that 50 coal mines had secured five-star ratings, of which 10 mines earned first, second and third positions with scores exceeding 93 per cent. He observed that these achievements reflect the commitment, leadership and disciplined efforts of the respective mining teams and provide valuable benchmarks for the wider sector. He congratulated all the recognised mines and acknowledged their contribution towards raising performance standards in coal mining.
Highlighting the way forward, Shri Jha stressed the importance of strengthening collaboration among coal companies and mining establishments through the exchange of knowledge, successful practices and practical solutions to common challenges. He called for a more integrated approach towards sector-wide improvement, wherein the achievements of individual mines serve as learning opportunities for others. He underscored that the Star Rating Programme should continue to evolve as a platform for collective learning and sustained progress, enabling the entire coal mining sector to achieve higher levels of performance, efficiency and responsible operations.
In his welcome address, Shri Satish Kumar, CCO emphasized that the Star Rating Awards Ceremony is a significant platform to recognise the exemplary performance of mines in safety, environmental management, scientific mining practices, productivity, and community welfare. He stated that these awards reflect the dedication and collective efforts of the mining community towards responsible and sustainable development of the coal sector.
Shri Satish highlighted that the Star Rating framework serves as an important benchmark for excellence, motivating mines to continuously improve operational standards while ensuring worker safety, environmental protection, land restoration, and the welfare of project-affected communities. He congratulated all award recipients and expressed confidence that their achievements would inspire others to adopt best practices and contribute to the nation’s vision of a self-reliant and developed India. He further said that the ceremony would encourage greater transparency, innovation, and accountability across the coal industry.
During the event, the winners and runners-up of the Hackathon on R&D 2026 were for their innovative solutions under the theme “NextGen AI for Smart Mining”. The winners included CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur; Technowave Solutions Private Limited, Ranchi, in association with IIT (ISM), Dhanbad; CSIR-CLRI, Chennai, in association with Dr Kalyan Sen & Associates Pvt. Ltd., Kolkata; and a consortium of CSIR-CMERI, Durgapur, C-DAC, Thiruvananthapuram, and M/s Unyrashapa Corporation Lord Tech, Ranchi, along with their respective first and second runners-up. The recognition celebrates their efforts in developing AI-driven solutions to address critical challenges in the coal sector, with a focus on enhancing operational efficiency, mine safety and environmental sustainability.
The Annual Star Rating Awards reflect the Ministry of Coal's continued commitment to promoting excellence, transparency and accountability in the coal mining sector. By recognising exemplary performance and encouraging the exchange of best practices, the programme seeks to strengthen a culture of continuous improvement and advance responsible, efficient and sustainable mining across the country.

title: WCL Emerges as Growth Engine of Coal India, Records Strong Growth in Production, Offtake and Overburden Removal
subtitle: Only CIL subsidiary to exceed targets in all three key parameters during April–October 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, has emerged as a key growth driver of Coal India Limited (CIL), recording strong performance across coal production, offtake and overburden removal during the current financial year. From April to October 2026, WCL was the
only subsidiary of CIL to exceed its targets in all three key operational parameters
, achieving 102.47% of its production target, 108.82% of its offtake target and 104.56% of its overburden removal target.
The company's strong operational performance has significantly contributed to strengthening domestic coal availability and supporting India's energy security. WCL's additional production of
4.53 MT
during April–October 2026 was higher than the entire net production growth of CIL during the corresponding period.
Strong Performance Across Key Parameters
WCL recorded particularly impressive growth during October 2026. Coal production increased to
5.93 MT
, compared with 3.60 MT during the corresponding month last year, registering a growth of
64.87%
, the highest among major CIL subsidiaries. The company also achieved 108.60% of its monthly production target.
Offtake during October increased to
6.67 MT
, against 4.44 MT in the corresponding month last year, registering a growth of
50.16%
. WCL was also the only major subsidiary to exceed its monthly offtake target, achieving 102.40%.
During the April–October period, WCL recorded:
32.96 MT coal production
, registering a growth of
15.92%
;
41.56 MT offtake
, registering a growth of
25.54%
; and
207.95 MCuM of overburden removal
, registering a growth of
36.10%
.
The company had also recorded the highest growth in both production and offtake among CIL subsidiaries during September 2026.
Record Stock Liquidation and Improved Coal Evacuation
A major achievement during the period has been WCL's substantial reduction in pithead coal stock. The stock was reduced from
13.034 MT on April 1, 2026 to 4.44 MT on October 31, 2026
, resulting in the liquidation of around
8.6 MT
, or approximately 66% of the opening stock.
Enhanced coordination with the Railways and focused monitoring of rake placement and loading contributed significantly to this achievement. WCL loaded
6,146 rakes
up to October 31, 2026, compared with 4,402 rakes during the corresponding period last year, registering an increase of
39.6%
.
Rake loading to the power sector increased by
40.8%
, while supplies to MAHAGENCO registered particularly strong growth.
Focused Monitoring and Mine-Level Decision Making
WCL's strong performance has been driven by intensive and continuous monitoring of operations at the mine level. Daily reviews of production, despatch and operational issues, regular meetings with Area General Managers, and frequent visits by senior management have enabled faster identification and resolution of operational bottlenecks.
The extension of monthly coordination and review mechanisms down to the mine level has strengthened accountability and ensured closer monitoring of critical activities across operations.
Close coordination with the Railways, State Governments and concerned Ministries has also facilitated the timely resolution of issues relating to environmental and forest clearances, land matters and other operational requirements.
During FY 2026–27, WCL has secured
four environmental clearances or amendments and two forest clearances
, helping ensure continuity of mining operations.
Technology, Quality and Operational Efficiency
WCL has continued to strengthen operational efficiency through improved transportation and loading infrastructure, including all-weather coal transportation roads, rapid loading systems and automated weighbridges.
The company currently has
six Surface Miners and three Continuous Miners in operation
. Focus on coal quality has also yielded positive results, with around
86% of sampled coal from April to October confirmed at its declared grade
.
Focused operational improvements have also contributed to a significant reduction in overloading charges, while October despatches achieved
100% net realisation without debit loss
.
Supporting Power Generation and Energy Security
The significant increase in WCL's offtake has directly supported power plants and industries. The additional coal supplies have strengthened domestic availability and contributed to reducing dependence on imported coal.
The additional rakes supplied to MAHAGENCO alone are estimated to have supported approximately
5,800 million units of additional power generation in Maharashtra
.
WCL's
Profit Before Tax for April–September 2026 stood at ₹1,352.26 crore
, registering a growth of
76.3%
over the corresponding period of the previous year.
Towards Aatmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat
WCL's performance during the current financial year demonstrates how focused leadership, intensive mine-level monitoring, faster decision-making and close coordination among stakeholders can translate into substantial operational outcomes.
With significant coal benches exposed in advance through record overburden removal, substantial reduction in pithead stocks, a motivated workforce and strong operational momentum, WCL is well positioned for sustained performance during the second half of the financial year.
WCL remains committed to powering the nation, strengthening India's energy security and contributing to the vision of an Aatmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.

content:
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, is implementing Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in official work across all offices.

title: TRAI issues the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today issued the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
To address the evolving needs related to the upgradation of grievance redressal framework, the Authority released a consultation paper on the Draft Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, on 7th May 2026, inviting comments and counter-comments by 12th and 19th June 2026, respectively. A total of 32 comments and 24 counter-comments were received from stakeholders and uploaded to the TRAI website. An online Open House Discussion (OHD) was held on 17th July 2026.
Based on the above consultations, the Authority has finalized the Amendment Regulations. The salient features of the same are given below:
The amended regulations shall apply to Internet Service Providers having more than ten thousand subscribers as on the last day of the preceding financial year. The existing alternative criterion based on annual financial turnover exceeding ₹5 crore has been dispensed with thus simplifying the applicability clause.
Consumers will now be able to register complaints and appeals, raise service requests, and make service-related queries through the service provider’s mobile application, in addition to the existing channels of the Complaint Centre, website and web portal thus giving wider choice, flexibility and ease to consumers in filing complaint and appeal.
Consumer support through Complaint Centres will be available round the clock on all days of the week, instead of the existing 16-hour arrangement. Such support may be provided through human representatives, automated systems, AI agents, other customer-centric technological solutions, or a combination thereof. Human assistance shall be available for at least sixteen hours daily. Technology-based solutions shall function with appropriate human oversight. This will ensure ease and convenience to consumers and gives flexibility to service providers in manning the Complaint Centres.
Every service provider shall equip dedicated desks or helplines in their Complaint Centre or Consumer support centres, with personnel or assistive technology capable of receiving calls from persons with disabilities (PwDs). Service providers will ensure that their mobile app, website and portal have accessibility features in accordance with the applicable guidelines or standards on accessibility for Persons with Disabilities issued by the Government of India.
The time limit for filing an appeal following disposal of a complaint has been revised from 30 days to 15 days as consumers would normally prefer appeal as soon as possible whereas a longer time allowed unduly increases compliance requirements. Consumers may now file appeals through the service provider’s mobile application, website or portal, in addition to the existing channels of email, post, in person, or through the Consumer Care Number. This will ensure faster resolution of appeal.
Also, the Appellate Authority has been made more responsible through the present amendment. It has been mandated that the Appellate Authority shall comprise one or more persons who are regular employees in the management of the service provider and also possess at least five years’ experience. The Appellate Authority shall examine the appeal, take appropriate action for resolution of the grievance, and communicate its final decision within 15 days of receipt of the appeal.
The earlier process of resolution of appeal cases through Advisory committee has been dispensed with in order to ensure efficient and time-bound resolution of appeal cases.
A new mechanism of “Feedback Survey” has been introduced. Upon resolution or closure of a complaint or appeal, the service provider shall conduct an online feedback survey to assess the consumer’s satisfaction with the resolution. Feedback shall be obtained on a five-point scale, ranging from “Fully Satisfied” (5 points) to “Totally Dissatisfied” (1 point). The service provider shall publish the results of such feedback surveys on its website on a quarterly basis.
It has also been mandated that every service provider shall place before its CEO or Board of Directors a quarterly report on the redressal of complaints, appeals and the results of feedback survey. This has been done to ensure suitable review and oversight of the disposal of complaints and appeals by the service providers at the highest level.
A new mechanism of Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee has been introduced. Every Service Provider shall establish a Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee to oversee and periodically review the functioning of its grievance redressal mechanism. The Committee shall comprise representatives of the Service Provider and at least one representative from each consumer organisation registered with the Authority in the State or Union Territory forming part of the licensed service area.  Service Providers will form such committee taking representation mandatorily from those states and union territories in which their subscriber base is above ten thousand. The Committee shall meet at least once every year to review the grievance redressal mechanism.
The amendment introduces a new mechanism of Regulatory Review. The Authority may conduct periodic review of the functioning of the Grievance Redressal Mechanism of the service providers by: -
audit and inspection of the records of the service provider,
audit and analysis of Quarterly Performance Reports submitted by the service provider,
review based on consumer feedback.
The amendment introduces the provision of financial disincentives in cases of disposal of complaint or appeal in contravention of the provisions of these regulations observed during the audit, inspection, analysis or review.
The provision of financial disincentives has also been introduced for non-submission/ delayed submission of the Quarterly Performance Report.
The amendments strengthen the consumer grievance redressal framework through enhanced digital access available to consumers, round the clock Complaint Centre support, improved accessibility for Persons with Disabilities and faster filing and disposal of complaints and appeals. The Appellate mechanism has been strengthened. Structured consumer feedback surveys, grievance redressal oversight committees, enhanced regulatory review, and financial disincentives for specified instances of non-compliance have been introduced to ensure appropriate supervision and compliance enforcement.
Full text of the Regulation is available on the TRAI's website

title: International Buddhist Confederation, in Collaboration with the Ministry of Culture and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, Organises International Conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” today at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 10:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The International Buddhist Confederation, New Delhi along with the Ministry of Culture, Government of India and Government of Arunachal Pradesh organised a day long international conference titled
“BUDDHISM: DISSEMINATION IN THE HIMALAYAN REGION AND BEYOND”
at the
Kalawangpo Convention Centre, Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
on today on the sidelines of the Sacred Relics Exposition in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh.
The conference was attended by monks, scholars, and delegates from India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Germany.
The Inaugural session commenced with
Mangalacharan
(Sacred chanting) by venerable sangha members followed by a welcome address by Secretary General IBC Shartse Khensur Jangchup Choeden Rinpoche. Addressing the gathering, the Secretary General IBC shed light on the theme of this conference which explores how Buddhism was born in the plains of India and spread across the subcontinent and beyond. He conveyed gratitude to the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh for gracing the occasion as the Chief Guest. The SG also expressed appreciation to Arunachal Pradesh administration and Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India for all the support rendered by them for convening the Conference.
The Secretary General IBC mentioned that the occasion holds special significance as it also marks the 14th founding day of the IBC during which the IBC has  continued to serve the Buddha Dhamma. He mentioned that IBC is committed to unite monastic and lay Buddhist organisations worldwide and expressed hope for future collaborations by IBC with the newly formed Arunachal Buddhist Confederation (ABC) in serving the cause of the Buddha Dhamma.
Addressing the conference, the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Guest at the occasion, congratulated the IBC on its 14th founding day, calling it a befitting coincidence that the International Conference on Buddhism being held in Tawang coincided with IBC’s glorious 14 years of service. He commended the efforts of IBC’s present and former leaders for their dedication and commitment towards Buddhism.
The Chief Minister commented that the conference, jointly organised by the IBC, the Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, holds special relevance in Tawang owing to the presence of the Sacred Relics. He noted the subject matter themes and subthemes of the discussions at the international conference and recalled how Buddhism that originated in India first transmitted due to efforts of King Ashoka in the 3rd century BCEt. He elaborated on how Buddhism, since the 6th and 7th CE, spread from Himalayan region of India, especially from Arunachal Pradesh, and reached Tibet and other regions attributing the same to Guru Padamasambhava and Shantarakshita. He also emphasized the importance of Tawang as the birth place of the 6th Dalai Lama.
Highlighting Arunachal Pradesh's special place in the larger Buddhist heritage, he said its monasteries are not merely places of worship but a spiritual and cultural legacy. He stressed on the need to ensure development and modernity while preserving cultural values, and to reflect on how the Buddha's message can be carried forward.
He concluded his remarks by thanking the Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India; National Museum; IBC; and Arunachal Pradesh administration for the Holy Relics Exposition and the International Conference. He also thanked the conference delegates, especially the international speakers from several countries, who have come to Tawang to participate in the conference.
The day-long conference featured three thematic sessions, focusing on various aspects of the dissemination, evolution and contemporary relevance of Buddhism in the Himalayan region and beyond.
Session One
During the first session of the conference, on
Carrying Forward the Buddha’s Legacy Post His Great Demise (Mahāparinirvāṇa),
the panel comprising speakers from
Sri Lanka, Myanmar and India
explored the Buddha’s enduring legacy following His Mahāparinirvāṇa (the Great Demise) through preservation of material heritage, ritual and institutional renewal. Discussions examined the Four Noble Truths as living heritage and Buddhism’s evolution as a composite cultural tradition shaped by cross-cultural exchange, international collaboration, and the transmission of the Dhamma across generations and societies.
Session Two
In the second session of the conference, on
Historical and Doctrinal Continuity of Buddhism,
speakers from
Nepal, Germany and India,
examined the transmission of Buddhist textual and monastic traditions through successive historical periods, with special emphasis on Arunachal Pradesh. It explored the diversity of Buddhist schools and their shared doctrinal foundations, highlighting the roles of language, interpretation, pedagogy and artistic expression in preserving and communicating Buddhist thought.
Session Three
In the last and final session of the day on
Buddhism and Right Livelihood,
the
panel of speakers from
Indonesia, Malaysia and India
, explored the relevance of Buddhist principles of Right Livelihood in contemporary academic, economic and social contexts. Discussions bridged the intellectual heritage of Nalanda with modern academia and examined cultural tourism, pilgrimage, sustainable prosperity, skill development, geographical interconnectedness and the implications of globalisation and consumerism through a Buddhist perspective.
The conference concluded with a Vote of Thanks by Shri Thupten Kalden, Director, Department of Karmik & Adhyatmik Affairs (DoKAA), Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The event culminated with the sacred Lamp Prayer of Atiśa Dīpaṃkara Śrījñāna, performed by the Monpa group, bringing the conference to a solemn and spiritually uplifting close.

title: Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha Arrive at Tawang Monastery; Exposition Marks a Significant Moment in Arunachal Pradesh's Buddhist Heritage
subtitle:
Sacred Piprahwa Relics brought to Tawang from the National Museum, New Delhi, for public veneration
Exposition to travel across Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai from 31 October to 21 November 2026

Initiative strengthens India's commitment to preserving and sharing its Buddhist civilisational heritage
date:

                02 NOV 2026 9:37AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The sacred Holy Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha from the National Museum, New Delhi, were ceremonially received by the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, at Tawang on 31st October, 2026, marking the commencement of a significant exposition of India's Buddhist heritage in Arunachal Pradesh. The sacred relics were accorded a traditional religious reception at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery), in the presence of Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, venerable Buddhist monks, religious leaders and devotees.
The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi. It will provide devotees and members of the public an opportunity to pay homage to the sacred relics across three important centres of Buddhist faith - Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai.
The inaugural programme at Tawang was attended by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism,
Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
, along with the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, venerable Buddhist monks, representatives of International Buddhist Confederation, other dignitaries and devotees.
In his message on the occasion,
Hon’ble
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
expressed happiness over the exposition of the Holy Relics of Bhagwan Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh, describing it as an occasion of immense spiritual and cultural significance. He highlighted the homecoming of the sacred Piprahwa Relics after more than a century as a moment of pride and joy, and expressed confidence that the exposition would further strengthen appreciation of India's rich Buddhist heritage and the universal teachings of Bhagwan Buddha.
The exposition holds special spiritual significance as it coincides with Lhabab Duchen, an important occasion in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition commemorating the Buddha's descent from the heavenly realm.
The sacred relics originate from Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh, an archaeological site associated with ancient Kapilavastu and the Shakya tradition of Lord Buddha. Preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, these relics hold immense historical, archaeological and spiritual significance for Buddhist communities.
An accompanying exhibition, titled
Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery
, will present the history of the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa, the significance of relic veneration and the journey of the Piprahwa heritage, including its repatriation to India.
The International Buddhist Confederation, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, will also organise an international conference titled “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” at the Kalawangpo Convention Hall, Tawang, on 2 November 2026.
The exposition will continue at Tawang Monastery from 1 to 7 November, followed by TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, from 8 to 13 November and the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from 14 to 20 November 2026. The sacred relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.
The exposition represents an important initiative to bring India's Buddhist heritage closer to communities in the North Eastern Region, while promoting the universal teachings of Bhagwan Buddha - peace, compassion, non-violence and harmony.
Through such initiatives, the Government of India continues its efforts to preserve, promote and disseminate the country's rich Buddhist heritage and strengthen India's historical and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities across the world.

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 NOV 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year.
Addressing the gathering, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the India Meteorology Department (IMD) had strengthened the weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban.
Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, Senior Scientist Suresh and others came specially from Delhi for the event.
MLA Padder-Nagseni Constituency and Leader of Opposition, J&K Legislative Assembly, Sh. Sunil Sharma; MLA of the Kishtwar Assembly Constituency and Ms. Shagun Parihar also spoke on the occasion. Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Sharma and SSP Kishtwar Sunny Gupta were also present among others.
The Minister said, the expansion of scientific and weather monitoring infrastructure has also strengthened the region's disaster preparedness in an area that is vulnerable to earthquakes, landslides and other weather-related challenges.
The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi. With the establishment of the new facility, Jammu and Kashmir now has four Seismological Observatories, including those at Jammu, Srinagar, Udhampur and Kishtwar.
Dr Jitendra Singh said the observatory would continuously monitor earthquake activity in the region and contribute to a better understanding of its seismic hazards. The information generated would also support the district administration and rescue teams in responding more effectively, besides helping in planning safer infrastructure.
Highlighting the transformation in meteorological infrastructure since 2014, Dr Jitendra Singh said that there was no Doppler Weather Radar coverage in the region earlier. After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities.
He further informed that four more Doppler Weather Radars are set to be commissioned in 2027 at Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla, further strengthening weather surveillance and extending coverage across the region.
The Minister also highlighted the significant expansion of the Automatic Weather Station network. From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12. These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region. He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas.
The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency. These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring.
Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts. The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information.
He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir. The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness. Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease.
Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon. He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings.
“Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories.
Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication. He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources.
Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas. He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them.
Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub. He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people.
The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Alias Lalan Singh
undertook a two-day visit to Sikkim during 2–3 November 2026 to review the progress of various initiatives and development programmes of the
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) in Sikkim of the North Eastern Region (NER).

Tingda Government Primary School,
interacted with students and encouraged them to pursue education and learning. He also visited the

North District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union Ltd (NDMU). Under White Revolution 2.0
at Mangan, marking an important step towards strengthening the dairy cooperative network and expanding organised dairy activities in North Sikkim. The initiative is expected to facilitate greater participation of dairy farmers in the cooperative network and strengthen institutional support for dairy development.
The Hon’ble Union Minister launched “
Minimum Standard Protocol for Semen Production and Standard Operating Procedures for Artificial Insemination Using Liquid Semen in Pigs”.
The publication establishes a standardised framework for semen production and artificial insemination (AI) using liquid semen in pigs. The protocols aim to promote scientific breeding practices, improve genetic quality, enhance productivity, strengthen biosecurity and expand the adoption of artificial insemination technology in pig farming.
The initiative is expected to improve reproductive efficiency, reduce the risk of disease transmission and enhance farmers' incomes, particularly in the North-Eastern Region, where pig rearing plays an important role in rural livelihoods.
The Hon’ble Union Minister also digitally launched the
Siri Cattle Conservation Programme,
aimed at conserving and promoting the indigenous Siri cattle breed, preserving valuable genetic resources and strengthening scientific breeding practices.

in Pakyong district. The proposed facility aims to strengthen the conservation of the indigenous Siri breed, support genetic improvement and promote scientific breeding and multiplication of quality germplasm.

During the address the Hon’ble Union Minister announced that DAHD, Government of India will establish a Centre of Excellence for the indigenous Siri cattle breed conservation and development in Sikkim. Hon’ble Union Minister directed for the preparation of a comprehensive Action Plan for Siri cattle conservation and development focusing on breed improvement, genetic conservation and scientific breeding. Further, he emphasised the need to prepare a Work Plan for introducing In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) technology to accelerate genetic improvement and facilitate the multiplication of superior germplasm.
The Hon’ble Minister congratulated on the inclusion of the North District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union Ltd. under White Revolution 2.0 and to ensure successful implementation, Hon’ble Minister advised National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) to prepare a comprehensive plan for the modernization of the dairy plant, expansion of the dairy cooperative network, and development of an integrated “Sikkim Milk” brand to drive sustainable growth of the dairy sector in the State.

content:
The Hon’ble Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh visited
Mangan
districts, Sikkim on
2nd
November 2026
to review fisheries development initiatives under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
